items.title: Compass Food Bank annual walk aims to raise $200,000 to help 2,000+ people weekly
items.summary: Participants at the 2025 annual walk event, which raised $178,000. The funds provided more than eight weeks of food and hygiene supplies for local students. The Compass Food Bank is organizing and hosting its 20th annual walk on Saturday, Sept. 19 in Mississauga. The event will take place at Church of St. Mark-Lutheran located at 130 Mineola Rd. E. m. to noon and will mark two decades of the organization’s community fundraising efforts, according to the food bank’s website. This year’s fundraising goal is $200,000. All proceeds will help provide food and hygiene items for individuals and families in south Mississauga who are experiencing food insecurity and are unhoused, according to the organizer. The initiative supports more than 2,000 individuals every week — one-third are children who rely on the service. The organization provides weekly access to food, according to the website. During the past 20 years, the walk has helped raise more than $750,000.

items.title: 280 vehicles stolen over a 30-day period in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Police crime data indicates there were 280 vehicles stolen in Mississauga and Brampton over the last 30 days. According to Peel Regional Police’s crime mapping tool, a combined 281 vehicle thefts occurred in Peel Region from Aug. 12 and Sept. 12, with 162 taking place in Mississauga, 118 in Brampton, and one in Caledon. Unlike previous reports, Peel Regional Police did not provide an updated breakdown of cases that had been solved, remained under investigation or were deemed unsolved. The crime map indicates that the vehicle thefts were mostly spread out between the two cities, with a noticeable cluster happening at Mississauga’s Pearson Toronto Airport. Vehicle thefts remain a common occurrence in the GTA — in recent news, four teens are collectively facing over 200 charges following an investigation into multiple stolen vehicles and commercial break-and-enters across Durham and the GTA. Between June and September 2026, the group was responsible for 36 incidents, including eight commercial break-and-enters and 15 vehicle theft-related offences involving stolen vehicles, attempted vehicle thefts, thefts from vehicles, and licence plate thefts. items.title: Mississauga man charged in car insurance fraud investigation
items.summary: A Mississauga man is facing charges in an ongoing fraud investigation, and police believe there may be other victims who have yet to come forward. Investigators allege that between April 2024 and August 2026, the accused sold fraudulent automobile insurance policies and knowingly provided victims with falsified proof of insurance documents across the GTA. “To date, police have identified 15 incidents connected to the scheme, with reported victim losses exceeding $10,000,” said Peel Regional Police. Police say he was previously licensed to sell insurance and had been employed by several insurance brokerages, and that he continued selling insurance policies after he no longer had the legal authority or licence to do so. 25-year-old Mississauga man Muhammad Raahim, was arrested on Wednesday, Aug. 26. He has since been released with conditions and is awaiting a future court appearance. “Members of the public are reminded to exercise caution when purchasing automobile insurance and to verify that insurance providers, brokers, and agents are properly licensed before making payments or relying on proof of coverage documents,” said police. Investigators believe there may be more victims, and are urging anyone who purchased automobile insurance through Raahim to contact Peel Regional Police’s Fraud Bureau at 905-453-2121, ext. 3335.

items.title: Inquest: Officer testifies about struggle with Mississauga man, 88, that turned fatal
items.summary: “I asked him to stop, indicating that he’s going to fall down the stairs, and he says, ‘That’s what I want to do’”: Const. Gord Middleton. Retired Mississauga schoolteacher John Brownlie, 88, dies in September 2023 following an interaction with a Peel Regional Police officer. This summary was produced using artificial intelligence and reviewed by an editor for accuracy and clarity. A Peel Regional Police officer testified Sept. 10 about the struggle that led to the fatal fall of 88-year-old John Brownlie, marking the third day of a coroner’s inquest into the Mississauga resident’s 2023 death. Const. Gord Middleton worked with the Crisis Outreach and Support Team (COAST), which pairs plain-clothes police officers with community-based crisis workers from the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) to support people experiencing mental health or addiction crises. Brownlie was identified as being appropriate for a COAST visit on Sept. 13, 2023 after his wife Doris called a crisis line a day earlier. “Information passed on to me was that she had called with concerns that Mr. Brownlie was not acting normally. He was aggressive. She was concerned for her safety,” Middleton said, noting Brownlie was also suspected of having a urinary tract infection.

items.title: Unlimited garbage collection is coming to Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon
items.summary: Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon residents looking to clear out some clutter will soon get another chance to put out unlimited amounts of acceptable garbage without garbage tags. But don’t make the mistake of thinking that means two weeks of unlimited garbage collection. Peel Region’s next garbage exemption period runs from Sept. 14 to 25, but each household’s exemption applies only on its regular garbage collection day. And that means residents need to pay attention to their collection schedule. If it’s your recycling day, the extra garbage will not be picked up. Peel Region says residents can put out unlimited amounts of acceptable garbage on their exemption day, with no garbage tags required. The Region advises residents to check their collection calendar to find their garbage pickup day. The exemption is a popular opportunity for residents doing a fall cleanup, cleaning out a garage or basement, or simply getting rid of accumulated household clutter. The exemption applies to acceptable household garbage that would normally go into the grey garbage cart.

items.title: Violent culprit follows, then robs shoppers at major Mississauga mall: police
items.summary: A culprit who’s believed to have followed customers from an electronics shop at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga before attacking and robbing them is being hunted by police. The latest incident, which occurred on Sept. , was the most violent of at least three similar muggings dating back to early May, Peel Regional Police said on Friday. A customer who had earlier bought an electronics product inside the large shopping mall was walking to their car in the parking garage when they were confronted by a male and robbed of their purchase. “During the incident, the victim sustained significant injuries and was transported to hospital,” police said in a news release. Officers with the Peel police 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau said two similar incidents occurred at Square One between May 9 and June 27. “In both instances, the suspect approached victims at their vehicles in the parking garage and forcibly took electronic products they had recently purchased,” police said, adding one of those victims sustained minor injuries. Investigators believe the same culprit is following customers who have purchased products from an electronics store and then approaching and robbing them in the shopping centre’s parking garage. As they hunt for the person responsible, police are reaching out to the public for help in identifying the culprit.

items.title: 17 candidates urged to meet residents as Mississauga city council race heats up
items.summary: With 17 candidates vying to become the new Ward 7 councillor in Mississauga, residents will have an opportunity to see and hear from many of those seeking the position at an all-candidates meeting being held on Monday night. With the current councillor, Dipika Damerla, entered in the mayoral race, that means a new face will join City of Mississauga council as Ward 7 representative for the next term, which begins following the Oct. 26 Ontario municipal election. Those organizing the upcoming candidates meeting said on Friday 10 of the 17 hopefuls seeking to succeed Damerla have so far confirmed their attendance. The event is being held on Sept. m. at the Royal Canadian Legion, Cooksville Branch #582 (456 Hensall Circle, just west of Cawthra Road and Dundas Street East). Organizers say the large field of Ward 7 candidates — the 17 entrants are the most in any of the city’s municipal election races — makes it even more important for residents to get a sense of what each person is promising to bring to the position. “This meeting will provide Ward 7 residents with an opportunity to meet the candidates in person, learn more about their platforms and ask questions about key issues” affecting both the ward and Mississauga, organizers said. ” Ward 7 includes the south-central part of Mississauga and is anchored by Cooksville.

items.title: Dig in: Community tree planting event advances Mississauga’s goal of one million trees by 2032
items.summary: Join City of Mississauga, TD representatives and volunteers to plant 525 native trees and shrubs for a greener city. Shovels in hand and saplings ready, the City of Mississauga is inviting residents to roll up their sleeves for TD Tree Days, an annual volunteer tree-planting program supported by TD Friends of the Environment Foundation that helps bring new life to local green spaces. Thanks to a grant from TD, the City will host three community tree-planting events in Mississauga starting September 19. Since launching its One Million Trees initiative in 2013, Mississauga has planted more than 650,000 trees. Placed end to end, they would roughly form a line long enough to stretch from Mississauga to Vancouver. Volunteers and TD representatives will gather to plant 525 native trees and shrubs in a single morning, making this one of the largest TD Tree Days events in Ontario in 2026. The event will help grow Mississauga’s urban forest and advance the City’s goal of planting one million trees by 2032. Trees are vital to our environment and well-being. They provide shade, habitat for birds and other wildlife, help reduce flooding and keep the city greener and more attractive. TD Tree Days works with local organizations and municipalities like City of Mississauga to create opportunities for people to come together, spend time outdoors and contribute to local green spaces. Free event. More details at TD Tree Days website.

items.title: Find your next favourite local business at Sourced in Sauga
items.summary: Discover and shop from IDEA Mississauga-supported businesses at Sourced in Sauga on Saturday, September 26. Business and innovation | September 11, 2026 IDEA Mississauga invites the community to Sourced in Sauga, a one-day celebration of local entrepreneurship presented in partnership with Square One Shopping Centre. This pop-up shopping experience brings together some of Mississauga’s most innovative entrepreneurs, artisans and small businesses for a day of discovery, connection and community. From childcare services and toy subscriptions to dog perfumes and handcrafted jewellery, there’s something for everyone. More information about how to register and the full list of vendors is available through the registration link on the Sourced in Sauga event page. Browse a diverse selection of locally made products and services, meet the entrepreneurs behind the brands and learn how IDEA Mississauga’s programs have helped support their growth and success. Shoppers will also have the chance to win one of two Square One gift cards valued at $250 each. So whether you’re looking for unique gifts, getting a head start on seasonal shopping, or simply exploring what Mississauga’s business community has to offer, Sourced in Sauga is an opportunity to support local entrepreneurs and discover something new. m. m.
